title: fix: guard null visibleRangeForPosition in indent guides (fixes #244370)
body:
### Summary Rendering indent guides crashes with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'left')` in `IndentsOverlay.prepareRender`. The code asserts `ctx.visibleRangeForPosition(...)!.left` non-null, but that method legitimately returns `HorizontalPosition | null` when the requested position is not in the currently rendered range (e.g. during scrolling, wrapped lines, or a stale layout). When it returns `null`, the `!` assertion dereferences null and throws, aborting the whole view render pass. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#244370 Recommended reviewer: `@hediet` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | [`78cb0b490a60`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/78cb0b490a60) | | Author | `@hediet` | | PR | (not identified) | | Message | Indent guides rendering (bracket pair guides) | | Why | This commit introduced the `ctx.visibleRangeForPosition(new Position(lineNumber, guide.column))!.left` expression at the crash site. The `!` non-null assertion bypasses the method's declared `HorizontalPosition \| null` return type; whenever the position is outside the rendered range the value is `null` and the dereference throws. This is a long-standing (pre-existing, 2022) latent bug rather than a recent regression. | > Pre-existing latent bug: `git blame` dates the offending line to 2022. Telemetry re-surfaces it intermittently because it only fires when `visibleRangeForPosition` returns `null` for a non-`-1` guide column during a render pass. ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant View as EditorView.render participant Overlay as IndentsOverlay.prepareRender participant Ctx as RenderingContext.visibleRangeForPosition View->>Overlay: prepareRender(ctx) Overlay->>Ctx: visibleRangeForPosition(Position(line, guide.column)) Note over Ctx: Returns null when the
position is not in the
rendered range Ctx-->>Overlay: null Note over Overlay: 💥 (null)!.left throws:
Cannot read properties of null ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/editor/browser/viewParts/indentGuides/indentGuides.ts` | crash site & root cause | L137-139 (from stack): `ctx.visibleRangeForPosition(new Position(lineNumber, guide.column))!.left` — `!` bypasses the nullable return | | `src/vs/editor/browser/view/renderingContext.ts` | producer (correctly typed) | L102-103: `visibleRangeForPosition(position): HorizontalPosition \| null { return this._viewLines.visibleRangeForPosition(position) ?? this._viewLinesGpu?.visibleRangeForPosition(position) ?? null; }` | ### Repro Steps Non-deterministic — depends on the renderer returning `null` for a guide column position while indent/bracket-pair guides are enabled. 1. Enable bracket pair / indentation guides (default). 2. Open a large file and scroll rapidly, or trigger a layout where a guide's column falls outside the currently rendered line range (wrapped lines, partially rendered viewport). 3. When `visibleRangeForPosition` returns `null` for a guide's column during `prepareRender`, the non-null assertion throws. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/editor/browser/viewParts/indentGuides/indentGuides.ts`: replace the `!.left` non-null assertion with an explicit null check. When `visibleRangeForPosition` returns `null` for a guide's column, `continue` to skip that single guide instead of dereferencing null. The method's declared return type is already `HorizontalPosition | null`, and the immediately surrounding code already treats null as a normal outcome (L132 uses `?.left ?? 0`; L152-154 uses `?.left ?? (left + this._spaceWidth)`). This makes the crash-site consumer honor the producer's already-correct nullable contract — the producer is not buggy, the `!` was an incorrect assertion — so the fix belongs at the assertion site, consistent with the existing null-tolerant handling in the same loop. **Alternatives considered**: using `?.left ?? leftOffset` to substitute a fallback offset — rejected because a wrong horizontal position would render a visibly misplaced guide, whereas skipping the guide (as `continue` does) simply omits a guide that cannot be positioned this frame; it will render correctly on the next layout pass. ### Recommended Owner `@hediet` — author of the original indent-guides rendering code (culprit commit `78cb0b490a60`) and current assignee of the issue; owner of the editor indent-guides area (`editor-indent-guides` label). > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/30472145297) · opus48 · 210 AIC · ⌖ 11.2 AIC · ⊞ 18.1K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests) --- > [!NOTE] > This was originally intended as a pull request, but the git push operation failed. > > **Original error:** The process '/usr/bin/git' failed with exit code 128 > > **Workflow Run:** [View run details and download bundle artifact](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/30472145297) > > The bundle file is available in the `agent` artifact in the workflow run linked above. title: ResolvedAuthority allows ports outside the valid TCP range
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->

<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: N/A

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: Current `main` branch
- OS Version: N/A

## Description

The `ResolvedAuthority` constructor validates that the supplied port is a nonzero integer, but it does not appear to validate that the port falls within the valid TCP port range.

The current check is:

    if (typeof port !== 'number' || port === 0 || Math.round(port) !== port) {
        throw illegalArgument('port');
    }

This rejects `0` and fractional values, but values such as `-1` and `65536` appear to pass the constructor validation.

## Relevant code path

A resolver can construct values such as:

    new vscode.ResolvedAuthority('localhost', -1);
    new vscode.ResolvedAuthority('localhost', 65536);

The accepted port is then used to create a `WebSocketRemoteConnection`.

That connection data is passed to `RemoteAuthorities.set(...)`, which stores the port without additional range validation.

The stored value is later used when constructing the remote resource authority:

    authority: `${host}:${port}`

This can produce invalid authorities such as:

    localhost:-1
    localhost:65536

## Expected behavior

`ResolvedAuthority` should reject port values outside the range `1` through `65535`.

## Possible validation

    if (
        typeof port !== 'number'
        || !Number.isInteger(port)
        || port < 1
        || port > 65535
    ) {
        throw illegalArgument('port');
    }

## Suggested tests

Constructor tests could cover:

- `-1`, rejected
- `0`, rejected
- `1`, accepted
- `65535`, accepted
- `65536`, rejected
- fractional values, rejected

title: Fix duplicate symlink decorations in the explorer
body:
Fixes #324389

The symlink `↷` decoration rendered multiple times next to each other on entries in the Files (explorer) view in the Agents window.

### Root cause

`ExplorerDecorationsProvider` was constructed and registered **per `ExplorerView` instance**, in `ExplorerView.setTreeInput`, guarded only by a field on that view.

`DecorationsService` keys its cached data per *provider instance* and merges every provider's letter into a single badge (`letters.join('', '')`). So each extra registration contributed another arrow — matching the issue screenshot showing `↷, ↷, ↷, ↷, ↷`.

In the classic workbench there is only ever one `ExplorerView`, so this never surfaced. In the Agents window the Files view is gated on `SessionHasWorkspaceContext` / `WorkspaceFolderCountContext`, so its view descriptor is removed and re-added as sessions are switched — every additional live `SessionsExplorerView` added another provider, and another arrow.

### Fix

The decorations are derived from the explorer *model*, not from a view, so the provider should be window-scoped rather than view-scoped:

- `ExplorerService.registerView` now registers the decorations provider exactly once (idempotent), owned by the service''s `DisposableStore`, so any number of explorer views share a single registration.
- `ExplorerDecorationsProvider` takes the explorer service as a plain constructor argument (before the service params) instead of via DI, so the service can construct it directly. Added a doc comment recording the single-registration requirement.
- `ExplorerView` no longer creates or registers a provider; the now-unused `IDecorationsService` dependency and field were removed.

The badge now renders exactly once regardless of how many explorer views a window has, and decorations stay correct as views come and go on session switches.

### Validation

- `tsc --project ./src/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — no errors in the touched areas.
- Hygiene passes (pre-commit hook).

Emit ARC telemetry for Agent Host file edits using the same tracking logic already used for local workbench Chat and Inline Chat edits.

The existing workbench ARC implementation is moved into a shared `EditArcTracker`. The workbench adapter now delegates to it, while Agent Host feeds tool edits and subsequent file changes into the same tracker.

No intended workbench behavior change:

- The existing `editTelemetry.reportEditArc` event name and payload remain unchanged.
- Inline completion telemetry (`editTelemetry.reportInlineEditArc`) is unaffected.

Local and Agent Host reporting share:

- The same ARC character calculation.
- The same inserted/deleted line calculations.
- The same 0/60/300-second sampling schedule.
- The same branch-change measurement.
- The same Microsoft telemetry contract and event name: `editTelemetry.reportEditArc`.

The input pipelines differ:

- Local tracking observes in-memory editor edits.
- Agent Host tracking reconciles tool edits with subsequent on-disk changes.

Agent Host additionally populates `provider`, `agentSessionId`, and `isSubagentSession`. For Copilot CLI sessions it also emits `vscode.editTelemetry.reportEditArc` to GitHub telemetry.

## Validation

- Existing local ARC fixture expectations remain unchanged.
- Parity tests compare the shared tracker and workbench adapter after each edit.
- Agent Host tests cover reconciliation, file deletion, branch changes, configuration changes, limits, and EOL changes.
- Manual Code OSS testing verified immediate and 60-second Agent Host ARC samples.

title: Allow configuring the content width of the experimental Markdown editor
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

## Feature request

Please make the content width of the experimental hybrid Markdown editor configurable.

VS Code 1.131 introduced the new `Markdown Editor (Experimental)` (view type `vscode.markdown.editor`). When this editor is used in a wide editor group, the rendered document remains centered in a column with a maximum width of approximately 900 px. The rest of the editor width is left unused.

This differs from the existing Markdown Preview, which can use the available editor width. The fixed narrow column is especially limiting for wide tables, code blocks, diagrams, and documents designed to make use of a large display.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use VS Code 1.131.0.
2. Open a `.md` file in a normal editor window.
3. Run **View: Reopen Editor With...** and select **Markdown Editor (Experimental)**.
4. Maximize the VS Code window or place the editor in a wide editor group.
5. Observe that the document content remains limited to roughly 900 px and is centered, leaving substantial unused space on both sides.

The same width limitation is present when the hybrid editor is opened in the Agents window, and in both Locked and Editing modes.

## Current implementation

In the bundled 1.131.0 Markdown editor code, the default `limitedWidth` value is `900`, and that value is applied to the `.md-editor-content` element as an inline `max-width`. There is currently no public setting that overrides it.

The existing `markdown.styles` setting only applies to the traditional Markdown Preview and does not affect `vscode.markdown.editor`.

## Proposed behavior

Add a user/workspace setting for the hybrid editor's maximum content width. For example, it could support:

- The current readable-width behavior as the default.
- A numeric pixel value for users who want a wider but still bounded document.
- A `full` or unlimited option that uses all available editor width, while retaining reasonable horizontal padding.

An example setting name could be `markdown.editor.maxContentWidth`, although the exact name and value format are not important to this request.

This should apply consistently in both normal editor windows and the Agents window.

## Why this is useful

A readable fixed width is a good default for prose, but Markdown is also commonly used for technical documents containing wide tables, long code blocks, Mermaid diagrams, and side-by-side comparisons. Allowing users to choose the width would preserve the current default while making the hybrid editor practical for these documents.

title: webview: consume Ctrl/Cmd+W and Ctrl/Cmd+N on desktop too
body:
# webview: consume Ctrl/Cmd+W and Ctrl/Cmd+N on desktop too

## What is broken

With a webview editor focused (Markdown preview, Release Notes, Simple Browser, any extension webview), a single <kbd>Cmd+W</kbd> closes **two** editor tabs. <kbd>Cmd+N</kbd> likewise opens **two** new tabs. Regular file tabs behave correctly, which is what makes this look like an extension bug rather than a core one.

It is intermittent in practice, because it depends on what has focus when the second dispatch lands.

## Root cause

A webview cannot let the workbench handle a key by itself. `handleInnerKeydown` in `pre/index.html` forwards the keydown to the host, and `webviewElement.handleKeyEvent` replays it:

```ts
// src/vs/workbench/contrib/webview/browser/webviewElement.ts
const emulatedKeyboardEvent = new KeyboardEvent(type, event);
Object.defineProperty(emulatedKeyboardEvent, 'target', { get: () => this.element });
this.window?.dispatchEvent(emulatedKeyboardEvent);
```

That is a **synthetic copy**. Whatever happens to it, the *real* event in the webview frame is untouched, so the real key stays unhandled and reaches the native menu. The menu has an accelerator for it, because `withKeybinding` in the main process looks up an accelerator per command id:

```ts
// src/vs/platform/menubar/electron-main/menubar.ts
withKeybinding(commandId, options) {
    const binding = typeof commandId === 'string' ? this.keybindings[commandId] : undefined;
    if (binding?.label) { if (binding.isNative !== false) { options.accelerator = binding.label; ... } }
    else { options.accelerator = undefined; }
}
```

`Cmd+W` is bound to `workbench.action.closeActiveEditor`, so *File > Close Editor* carries a `Cmd+W` accelerator. Triggering it sends `vscode:runKeybinding` back to the renderer, which dispatches the command a **second** time:

```ts
// src/vs/platform/keybinding/common/abstractKeybindingService.ts
public dispatchByUserSettingsLabel(userSettingsLabel: string, target: IContextKeyServiceTarget): void {
    this._log(`/ Dispatching keybinding triggered via menu entry accelerator - ${userSettingsLabel}`);
    ...
    this._doDispatch(keybindings[0], target, false);
}
```

By then the first dispatch has already closed the active tab and moved focus to the next one, so the second dispatch closes **that** tab.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant WV as Webview frame
    participant WB as Workbench renderer
    participant M as Native menu (main)

    U->>WV: Cmd+W (real event)
    WV->>WB: postMessage 'did-keydown'
    WB->>WB: replay synthetic KeyboardEvent
    WB->>WB: closeActiveEditor -> closes tab A, focus moves to B
    Note over WV: real event was never preventDefault'd
    WV-->>M: unhandled key reaches the native menu
    M->>WB: vscode:runKeybinding 'cmd+w'
    WB->>WB: dispatchByUserSettingsLabel -> closeActiveEditor -> closes tab B
```

**Why a regular editor is fine.** The keybinding service consumes the real event when a binding matches, so the key never reaches the menu:

```ts
// src/vs/workbench/services/keybinding/browser/keybindingService.ts
const shouldPreventDefault = this._dispatch(keyEvent, keyEvent.target);
if (shouldPreventDefault) {
    keyEvent.preventDefault();
}
```

## The fix

These two keys were already consumed for the PWA case in #164981 (for #150735), just gated behind `!onElectron`. The desktop failure mode is different but the remedy is the same, so the gate is dropped for the two keys the workbench binds itself. `F1` and `F5` stay web-only, since those are browser actions rather than menu accelerators.

```diff
-			} else if (!onElectron && (isCloseTab(e) || isNewWindow(e) || isHelp(e) || isRefresh(e))) {
-				// Prevent Ctrl+W closing window / Ctrl+N opening new window in PWA.
+			} else if (isCloseTab(e) || isNewWindow(e)) {
+				// Prevent the platform from acting on a key the host already handles.
+				// ...
 				e.preventDefault();
+			} else if (!onElectron && (isHelp(e) || isRefresh(e))) {
+				// Prevent F1 opening browser help / F5 reloading the PWA.
+				e.preventDefault();
 			}
```

### AltGr is excluded

`isCloseTab` and `isNewWindow` test `e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey`, and AltGr reports as Ctrl+Alt on Windows and Linux. Consuming those keys on desktop without a guard would therefore swallow AltGr+W and AltGr+N, so a layout that types a character there (n-acute on Polish, for instance) would lose that input in every desktop webview. The condition moved into a named predicate that ignores Alt and the AltGraph modifier:

```js
function isHostBoundShortcut(e) {
	if (e.altKey || e.getModifierState('AltGraph')) {
		return false;
	}
	return isCloseTab(e) || isNewWindow(e);
}
```

The web path had this hazard already, so the guard fixes that case too. Both combinations are covered as negative test cases.

### The CSP hash had to be updated

`pre/index.html` pins a `sha256` of its own inline script in its CSP, and that hash is maintained by hand rather than generated by the build. Editing the script without updating the hash makes the CSP block it, and then **no webview loads at all**. The hash in this PR is recomputed accordingly:

```
script bytes : 39448
old hash     : sha256-FFQoOVVa2tOE3uqUvirwaMNT20TZmrHcL2aaOjJ8BUo=
new hash     : sha256-nwlicgcSw6Z8ipNjNsUx5rOAD+Ua8UrTuM5dfV8OCIE=
```

Worth knowing for reviewers: the added test also guards this, since a blocked script prevents nothing and the test fails.

## Test

`extensions/vscode-api-tests` gains a case that dispatches keydowns inside a real webview and asserts which ones the webview consumes. It is safe to run because untrusted (script dispatched) events are never forwarded to the workbench (`shouldForwardKeyEvent` requires `isTrusted`), so it exercises `handleInnerKeydown` without actually closing the panel under test.

It includes a **negative case** (`plain a`) so an over-broad fix that prevents everything cannot pass.

## Before and after

Verified against a shipped **1.130.0** desktop build, patching only the webview bootstrap, using a standalone copy of the same assertion as the committed test so it could run without a source build. Same binary, same isolated profile, same harness. Only the change differs.

Three states were measured, so the AltGr guard is shown to be load-bearing rather than assumed.

**1. Unpatched, the reported bug**

```text
VS Code 1.130.0 (Desktop)
FAIL  ctrl+w   defaultPrevented=false  expected=true
FAIL  meta+w   defaultPrevented=false  expected=true
FAIL  ctrl+n   defaultPrevented=false  expected=true
FAIL  meta+n   defaultPrevented=false  expected=true
PASS  altgr+w  defaultPrevented=false  expected=false
PASS  altgr+n  defaultPrevented=false  expected=false
PASS  plain a  defaultPrevented=false  expected=false
failures: 4          exit code: 1
```

**2. Consuming the keys without the AltGr guard, to confirm the hazard is real**

```text
PASS  ctrl+w   defaultPrevented=true   expected=true
PASS  meta+w   defaultPrevented=true   expected=true
PASS  ctrl+n   defaultPrevented=true   expected=true
PASS  meta+n   defaultPrevented=true   expected=true
FAIL  altgr+w  defaultPrevented=true   expected=false
FAIL  altgr+n  defaultPrevented=true   expected=false
PASS  plain a  defaultPrevented=false  expected=false
failures: 2          exit code: 1
```

**3. This PR**

```text
PASS  ctrl+w   defaultPrevented=true   expected=true
PASS  meta+w   defaultPrevented=true   expected=true
PASS  ctrl+n   defaultPrevented=true   expected=true
PASS  meta+n   defaultPrevented=true   expected=true
PASS  altgr+w  defaultPrevented=false  expected=false
PASS  altgr+n  defaultPrevented=false  expected=false
PASS  plain a  defaultPrevented=false  expected=false
failures: 0          exit code: 0
```

State 1 reproduced identically on three consecutive runs. State 2 is what the added AltGr cases exist to catch.

### Independent confirmation that the accelerator path is real

While automating this, a launched window that was frontmost but not the key window still closed a tab on `Cmd+W`, even though the renderer received no keydown at all. That isolates the second dispatch: with the renderer path inert, the native menu accelerator alone still closes an editor.

The keybinding troubleshooting log shows both dispatches for one keypress, ~8 ms apart (`Developer: Toggle Keyboard Shortcuts Troubleshooting`):

```
14:58:19.814 [KeybindingService]: + Invoking command workbench.action.nextEditor.
14:58:19.821 [KeybindingService]: / Dispatching keybinding triggered via menu entry accelerator - alt+cmd+right
14:58:19.822 [KeybindingService]: + Invoking command workbench.action.nextEditor.
```

## Manual repro

1. Open four files so there are several tabs.
2. Open a webview editor, for example *Markdown: Open Preview*.
3. Focus the webview tab.
4. Press <kbd>Cmd+W</kbd> once.

Before: two tabs close. After: one tab closes.

## Scope note

The same double dispatch applies to any shortcut whose command is also a menu item. `Cmd+Alt+Left/Right` skipping two tabs is the same root cause. This PR deliberately covers only the two keys that already had `isCloseTab` and `isNewWindow` helpers, to keep the change small. A general fix would need the webview to know which keys the workbench has bound.

## Downstream reports

Users hit this through extension webviews, where it reads as an extension bug. anthropics/claude-code#29631 collects several independent reports with the same trace.


## Verification against the linked issues

@dmitrivMS asked whether the two issues I listed are actually fixed. Here is what I can and cannot show.

### What is verified

The change consumes the real event on desktop. Running this PR's integration test with `main`'s `pre/index.html` in place, the four combos come back un-consumed, and with this branch they are consumed:

```
      -    "defaultPrevented": false      +    "defaultPrevented": true    ctrl+w
      -    "defaultPrevented": false      +    "defaultPrevented": true    meta+w
      -    "defaultPrevented": false      +    "defaultPrevented": true    ctrl+n
      -    "defaultPrevented": false      +    "defaultPrevented": true    meta+n
```

Full matrix on desktop (`onElectron = true`):

| key combo | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `Cmd+W`, `Ctrl+W` | passes to platform | **consumed** |
| `Cmd+N`, `Ctrl+N` | passes to platform | **consumed** |
| `Ctrl+Tab`, `Ctrl+Shift+Tab` | passes to platform | passes to platform |
| `Cmd+Alt+Right` (default mac `nextEditor`) | passes to platform | passes to platform |
| `AltGr+W`, `AltGr+N` | passes to platform | passes to platform |
| `Cmd+C`, `Cmd+S` | consumed | consumed |
| `F1`, `F5` | passes to platform | passes to platform |
| plain `a` | passes to platform | passes to platform |

On web the matrix is unchanged except `AltGr+W` and `AltGr+N`, which go from consumed to passed. That is the intended AltGr guard so layouts that type a character with those combos keep the input, but it is a change on the web path rather than a no-op, so I would rather call it out than bury it.

### What is not verified

I could not reproduce #270722 against `main`, so I cannot claim this PR fixes it.

I built `main` and drove a real <kbd>Cmd+W</kbd> at a focused extension webview panel with two other editors open. The webview received a trusted `keydown` (`isTrusted: true`, `keyCode: 87`, `metaKey: true`) and did not consume it, and File > Close Editor does carry a `Cmd+W` accelerator in that build (`AXMenuItemCmdChar=W`, no extra modifiers). Every precondition in my root-cause description above was satisfied. Exactly one tab closed.

A likely explanation is that the re-dispatch path is already guarded on `main`:

```ts
// webviewElement.ts
private shouldForwardKeyEvent(event: KeyEvent): boolean {
    return event.isTrusted || !!this._content.options.forwardUntrustedKeypressEvents;
}
private handleKeyEvent(type: 'keydown' | 'keyup', event: KeyEvent) {
    if (!this.shouldForwardKeyEvent(event) || !this.isActiveElement()) {
        return;
    }
```

Those guards landed in c74dbf449ec (2026-06-03) and 0a43759b446 (2026-06-05), both well after #241801 (Feb 2025) and #270722 (Jul 2025) were filed. So the double dispatch those issues describe may already be mitigated on `main` and only reproduce on released builds.

That does not make this change wrong. Consuming a key the workbench binds itself is still the correct behavior for the webview, and it is what keeps the platform from acting on it in a PWA. But I do not want to attach a fixes claim I cannot demonstrate, so I would treat this as hardening unless someone can reproduce the double close on current `main`.

title: Agent Host session customizations are not scoped to the session's working directory in multi-root workspaces
body:
## Summary

In the **Editor Window**, Agent Host session customizations are **not scoped to the session's working directory**. When a **multi‑root workspace** (more than one folder) is open, every Agent Host session receives customizations aggregated from **all** workspace folders — instructions, prompts, skills, agents, hooks, **and** MCP servers configured in VS Code — regardless of which folder that session actually selected as its primary/working directory.

So if you open a multi‑root workspace with folders A and B and create/resume a session anchored to folder A, that session also gets folder B's customizations and MCP servers. That is wrong: a session's customizations should follow the session's own working directory (or directories), not the whole window's set of folders.

> Note: this is an **existing** behavior, independent of any in‑flight work.

## Scope / preconditions

- **Editor Window** (not the Agents window).
- A **multi‑root workspace** with **more than one folder** open.
- Applies to Agent Host sessions (e.g. Copilot Agent Host).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have two folders, A and B, each with its own customizations (e.g. `.github/instructions`, skills/agents, and MCP servers in `.vscode/mcp.json`).
2. Open a **multi‑root workspace** containing both A and B in the Editor Window.
3. Create or **resume** an Agent Host session and pick folder A as its working directory.
4. Inspect the customizations/MCP servers available to that session.

## Expected

The session sees only the customizations and MCP servers relevant to **its own working directory** (folder A), not folder B's.

## Actual

The session sees customizations and MCP servers from **all** workspace folders (A **and** B) — instructions/prompts/skills/agents/hooks **and** MCP servers configured in VS Code (`.vscode/mcp.json`, user, remote).

## Root cause

The Agent Host customization sync is computed **per harness (session type), not per session**, and enumerates the workspace **globally**:

- The active‑client customization refs are resolved once per harness in [`resolveCustomizationRefs`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostLocalCustomizations.ts) and registered via `registerForAgent(sessionType)` in `agentHostActiveClientService.ts`. The resulting bundle is broadcast to **every** active session of that harness via `session/activeClientSet`.
- File‑based customizations come from `enumerateLocalCustomizationsForHarness`, which lists prompt files across the workspace storage sources (all folders) with no per‑session working‑directory filter.
- MCP servers come from `collectNonPluginMcpServers`, which iterates the global `IMcpService.servers` (all folders) — `.vscode/mcp.json`, user, and remote — again with no per‑session working‑directory filter.

Because the bundle is per‑harness and workspace‑wide, a session whose working directory is a single folder (or a folder outside the workspace, or a workspace‑less/scratch session) still receives customizations and MCP servers aggregated from all workspace folders.

## Impact

- Customizations and MCP servers leak across folders into sessions that are not scoped to them.
- In a multi‑root workspace, a session anchored to one folder can pick up unrelated (and potentially heavier or sensitive) MCP servers and instructions from other folders.

## Suggested direction

Scope the synced customizations/MCP servers to the session's working directory set (index 0 = primary, plus any additional roots the session actually spans) rather than to all workspace folders. This likely requires making the customization resolution session‑aware rather than purely per‑harness.

title: Fix agent host diff file paths
body:
Fixes two problems with the file paths shown when diffing agent host changes (e.g. from the changes pill in the Session chat input toolbar).

### 1. `.../<toolCallId>/.../before/<file>` on the original side

`session-db:` content URIs have two layouts. The legacy one encoded everything in the URI path:

```
session-db://<hexSessionUri>/<toolCallId>/<hexFilePath>/before/<basename>
```

The current layout puts the real file path in the path and the lookup fields in the query, but legacy URIs are still parsed for backwards compatibility, so old sessions leak that shape into the UI. It also made the multi diff row render as a rename (`R` badge plus a struck through path), because a row is flagged as renamed whenever `modifiedUri.path !== originalUri.path`.

New `canonicalizeSessionDbUri` rewrites legacy URIs into the current layout, applied at the single consuming choke point `normalizeFileEdit` so the changes view, chat response file changes and the pill diff all benefit. The URI helpers moved from `node/shared/fileEditTracker.ts` into a new common module so browser code can use them.

### 2. `/c:/Code/...` next to `C:\Code\...` for the same file

The paths were already identical; only the labels differed. The `file:` side renders via `fsPath` plus drive letter normalization, while the wrapped `vscode-agent-host:` side went through a formatter of `{ label: '${path}', separator: '/' }` with no drive letter normalization. (The lower cased drive comes from `URI.toString()`, which always lower cases it.)

- New `agentHostLabelFormatter(authority, os)` produces OS native formatting and is registered for the `local` authority with the client OS, since the in-process host always runs on this machine.
- The scheme wide fallback, used by remote hosts whose OS the protocol does not report, gains `normalizeDriveLetter: true`. That is safe cross platform because it only fires when `label[2] === ':'`. It deliberately keeps `/`, as hardcoding `\` would corrupt a Linux or WSL host's paths when viewed from a Windows client.

| URI | label |
| --- | --- |
| local (Windows) | `C:\Code\repo\src\app.ts` |
| remote, OS unknown, Windows path | `C:/Code/repo/src/app.ts` |
| remote, OS unknown, posix path | `/home/user/repo/src/app.ts` |

### Testing

New unit tests for `canonicalizeSessionDbUri` and for all three label cases above. The existing agent host URI, filesystem provider and file edit diff suites still pass.

title: chat: fix BYOK tool schemas and continuation state
body:
## What

Fixes the Gemini BYOK function-declaration converter so it correctly handles JSON Schema tool parameters that use nullable **type arrays** (e.g. `{ "type": ["string", "null"] }`).

## Why

The converter in `geminiFunctionDeclarationConverter.ts` assumed a schema `type` was always a single string. When a tool parameter used a nullable union, the array was stringified into `"string,null"` and thrown as:

```
Unsupported type: string,null
```

Through the Agent Host BYOK path this surfaced as an HTTP `502` that the Copilot SDK retried **five times** (~35s) before failing the turn. It was reproduced with `gemini/models/gemini-3.5-flash` and a set of connected MCP servers whose tool schemas contain nullable parameters.

Notably, calling the Gemini OpenAI-compatible REST endpoint directly with `["string", "null"]` **succeeds** — Gemini accepts nullable unions. The failure was entirely in our shared client-side converter, so regular editor BYOK is susceptible to the same schema shape, not just the Agent Host.

## What changed

The property/array transform in `toGeminiFunction` was rewritten around two helpers:

- `collectAlternatives` recursively flattens `anyOf`/`oneOf` **and** nullable `type` arrays into a flat list of concrete, non-null alternatives, tracking whether `null` appeared anywhere (per branch, at any position).
- `transformConcrete` builds a single Gemini `Schema` for one flattened alternative.

Resulting behavior:

- Nullable unions (`["string", "null"]`) map to `{ type: STRING, nullable: true }`.
- Multi-type unions (`["string", "number", "null"]`) map to a Gemini `anyOf` with `nullable: true`.
- `anyOf`/`oneOf` map to Gemini's native `Schema.anyOf`, preserving **all** alternatives (previously only the first was kept). Combined shapes like `anyOf: [{ type: ["string","null"] }, { type: "number" }]` now keep `number` and stay nullable regardless of branch order.
- Nullable **array items** and object properties are handled recursively.
- `null` is removed inside each branch before nullability is decided, fixing two bugs: silently dropping a real alternative, and losing nullability when the null branch is not first.
- Replaced the `any`-typed transform with a typed recursive `Schema` builder.

`allOf` has no Gemini equivalent and is still approximated by its first subschema (documented inline).

## Tests

31 unit tests, including:

- Nullable type arrays, nullable array items/containers, nullable objects (properties + `required` preserved), nullable + `enum`, and deep nested nullability.
- `anyOf`/`oneOf` preserving all alternatives; combined nullable-union shapes in both branch orders; all-`null` union collapsing to `NULL`.
- Safety guards: an unknown scalar type throws a clean single-type error; an unknown type inside a union names one offending type (never `string,garbage`); and an invariant that the converter never emits a key outside Gemini's `Schema`, even when the input carries unsupported keywords (`format`, `$ref`, `additionalProperties`, `min*/max*`).

## Notes for reviewers

- Targeted fix that keeps the existing "sanitize to Gemini's Schema subset" behavior. A larger follow-up worth considering separately: pass raw JSON Schema through the SDK's `FunctionDeclaration.parametersJsonSchema` (mutually exclusive with `parameters`) so Gemini's backend does the conversion and this converter can be removed — but that needs live-model validation and could surface different unsupported-keyword rejections.
- Gemini-supported constraint keywords (`format`, `minimum`/`maximum`, `pattern`, `minItems`/`maxItems`, ...) are currently dropped rather than forwarded; the invariant test documents this. Forwarding them (with the string-typed `minItems`/`maxItems` coercion Gemini expects) is a possible follow-up.

title: Support loading MCP servers from all workspace folders (multi-root)

labels.name: workbench-multiroot
labels.description: Multi-root (multiple folders) issues

body:
Summary

Currently MCP servers are discovered only for a single workspace folder. In multi-root workspaces the product only loads customizations (instructions/skills/agents) from the primary working directory by default; MCP server discovery follows the same single-folder behavior. For provisional sessions VS Code may list MCP servers, but those lists are also limited to a single folder.

Proposal

Support loading and listing MCP servers from all workspace folders in multi-root workspaces.

Rationale

- Consistency: Other local agents (Copilot, Claude, local agent) and existing multi-root behavior aim to load instructions/skills/agents from multiple workspace folders. MCP server discovery should follow the same approach.
- Usability: Users working in multi-root workspaces expect servers declared in any workspace folder (including workspace-specific .mcp.json files and .vscode/mcp.json) to be available when creating sessions.
- Provisional sessions: Use available SDK APIs (e.g., Copilot SDK discovery/listing if available) to include MCP servers from all workspace folders for provisional sessions as well.

Acceptance criteria

- MCP servers declared in any workspace folder are discoverable and listed in the MCP servers picker when a multi-root workspace is open.
- Workspace-specific .mcp.json and .vscode/mcp.json files from all workspace folders are honored and their servers included.
- Provisional sessions include MCP servers discovered from all workspace folders (using Copilot SDK discovery/listing where applicable).
- Duplicate servers are de-duplicated in UI lists.
- Behavior is configurable or documented (if there are cases where only the primary folder should be used, document rationale and opt-out).

Implementation notes

- Update MCP server discovery logic to iterate over all workspace folders and aggregate servers from each folder's configuration (.mcp.json, .vscode/mcp.json, etc.).
- When creating sessions, allow manually specifying mcpServers for the session and ensure servers from all workspace folders can be included.
- For provisional sessions, investigate and use the Copilot SDK (or equivalent) API for discovery/listing if available.
- Present servers grouped by workspace folder in the UI (or clearly show source folder) to make it obvious where each server is declared.

Link to discussion/context

This request is based on internal discussion about multi-root behavior for MCP servers and aligning with how local agents manage multi-root loading of instructions/skills/agents.

title: Autopilot stops on a text-only response without calling task_complete
body:
* Copilot Chat Extension Version: Built into VS Code 1.130.0
* VS Code Version: 1.130.0 (user setup), commit `1b6a188127eeaf9194f945eb6eb89a657e93c54c`
* OS Version: Windows_NT x64 10.0.19045
* Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agent mode with Autopilot
* Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): `GPT 5.6 Luna`
* Logs:

```text
2026-07-29 12:14:37.694 [info] [ToolCallingLoop] Stop hook result: shouldContinue=false, reasons=undefined
2026-07-29 12:14:37.694 [info] [ToolCallingLoop] Autopilot: model produced a text-only response, treating as done
```

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Start a Copilot Chat session in Agent mode and enable Autopilot.
2. Give the agent a multi-step task and let it return an intermediate text-only response without calling `task_complete`.

Expected behavior:

If the task is unfinished and `task_complete` was not called, Autopilot should continue working by sending its internal continuation prompt.

Actual behavior:

Autopilot treats the non-empty text-only response as completion and stops.

This appears to correspond to the following condition in `ToolCallingLoop.shouldAutopilotContinue()`:

```ts
if (result.round.toolCalls.length === 0 && result.round.response.trim().length > 0) {
    this._logService.info(
        '[ToolCallingLoop] Autopilot: model produced a text-only response, treating as done'
    );
    return undefined;
}
```

This seems inconsistent with the standard Autopilot completion protocol, where `task_complete` is the completion signal and the model should otherwise receive a continuation nudge.

title: Inline suggestions suppress the suggest widget entirely: no completion request is ever sent while typing
body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: **Yes** (the provider is built-in, so "Disable All Extensions" does not turn it off)

- VS Code Version: 1.130.0
- OS Version: macOS (Darwin 25.5.0, Apple Silicon)

### Summary

With Copilot AI features enabled, the IntelliSense suggest widget never opens while typing an identifier. The editor does not merely hide the widget — it never issues a completion request to the language server at all.

This is not TypeScript-specific in principle, but TypeScript makes it easy to prove, because `tsserver` logs every request it receives.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a TypeScript React project (React + `@types/react` installed).
2. Ensure Copilot AI features are enabled (default in 1.130).
3. In a `.tsx` file, inside a component, type `useSt` on a blank line.

**Expected:** the suggest widget opens and offers `useState` as an auto-import from `react`.

**Actual:** ghost text appears, and no suggest widget is shown. `useState` is never offered, so the auto-import never happens.

Typing `React.` *does* open the widget and works correctly — trigger characters take a different code path.

### Evidence that no request is sent

With `"typescript.tsserver.log": "verbose"`, then `TypeScript: Open TS Server Log`, and correlating the `change` requests (which record the exact keystrokes) against `completionInfo` requests:

- Typing `String` then `.` → one `completionInfo` with `"triggerCharacter": ".", "triggerKind": 2`. Works.
- Backspacing through `String` → `completionInfo` with `triggerKind: 1`, refiltering the already-open widget. At the empty prefix this response contains 781 auto-import entries **including** `{"name": "useState", "source": "react", "hasAction": true}`.
- Typing `useEffe` from scratch (seq 142–157) → **zero** `completionInfo` requests.
- Typing `useSt` from scratch (seq 189–198) → **zero** `completionInfo` requests.

The last `completionInfo` in the log is seq 110, while typing continues to seq 198. So the language server is never asked. When it *is* asked, it returns the correct completion.

Verified independently that the language service is healthy: driving `ts.createLanguageService` with the same `tsconfig.json` and calling `getCompletionsAtPosition` returns `useState` with `source: "react"` under both `includePackageJsonAutoImports: "on"` and `"auto"`.

### Workaround

**Disable AI Features** from Copilot Chat. IntelliSense returns immediately; ghost text disappears. Re-enabling AI features reproduces the bug immediately. The narrower `"github.copilot.editor.enableAutoCompletions": false` also works.

There appears to be no configuration where both inline completions and the suggest widget are available.

### Notes

- `editor.inlineSuggest.suppressSuggestions` defaults to `false`, and setting it explicitly to `false` does **not** fix this — which is what makes this look like a bug rather than intended behavior.
- `editor.quickSuggestions` is at its default (`other: "on"`) and unmodified.
- A clean profile (`code --profile clean-test`) works correctly, but only because AI features are inactive there. Copying the full user settings into that clean profile does **not** reproduce the bug, confirming this is not settings-related.
- `code --list-extensions` does not list built-in extensions, so Copilot is invisible there; this makes the cause easy to misattribute.
- This is the same shape as #131940 (IntelliCode whole-line completions suppressing the suggest widget).

title: Fix Agents window shell CSS specificity
body:
## Problem

Several Agents window shell rules tied shared base/workbench selectors on specificity, so stylesheet concatenation order decided the rendered result.

| Surface | Intended rule | Equal-specificity competitor | Order-dependent property |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sidebar action placeholder | `.sidebar-action > .action-label` | `.codicon[class*='codicon-']` | `display: none` versus `inline-block` |
| New Chat tab button | `.chat-composite-bar-new-chat .action-item .action-label` | `.monaco-action-bar .action-item .codicon` | `width`/`height: 26px` versus `16px` |
| Read-only lock and in-progress indicator | tab-local codicon selectors | `.monaco-workbench .codicon[class*='codicon-']` | compact `font-size: 12px` versus `16px` |
| Rename input | `.chat-composite-bar-tab-input.monaco-inputbox .input` | `.monaco-inputbox > .ibwrapper > .input` | `padding: 0 4px` versus `4px 6px` |
| Command-center title icon | title-icon selector | `.monaco-workbench .codicon[class*='codicon-']` | unsupported `font-size: 14px` versus `16px` |

## Change

The first four cases add the smallest semantic owner needed to break the tie. Each non-obvious selector has an inline comment naming the competing selector and affected property.

The title icon is handled differently: codicons support only base 16px and compact 12px sizes, so it now uses `var(--vscode-codiconFontSize)`. Because that agrees with the shared workbench rule, no extra selector specificity is needed. This intentional 14px → 16px correction accounts for the two titlebar screenshot changes reported by CI.

## Validation

- `npm run stylelint -- src/vs/sessions/browser/media/sidebarActionButton.css src/vs/sessions/browser/parts/media/chatCompositeBar.css src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/media/sessionsTitleBarWidget.css`
- `npm run precommit`
- Rendered 54 chat composite bar, session header, titlebar, pull-request, and changes fixtures in product and reversed stylesheet order: exact image hashes match with no render errors

title: Fix Quick Input action visibility specificity
body:
## Problem

Quick Input row actions are hidden until their row is hovered, focused, selected, or marked `always-visible`. The old idle selector

```css
.quick-input-list .quick-input-list-entry-action-bar .action-label
```

had specificity `(0,3,0)`. Icon actions and icon toggles also match the shared action-bar rule

```css
.monaco-action-bar .action-item .codicon
```

which has the same specificity and sets `display: flex`. When the shared action-bar stylesheet loaded later, idle row controls became visible.

## Change

Adds the owning `.quick-input-list-entry` to the two idle selectors. That raises the hidden state to `(0,4,0)`, while the existing hover, focus, selected-row, and `always-visible` selectors remain more specific and continue to reveal the controls on intent. The CSS comment records this cascade contract beside the rule.

## Validation

- `npm run stylelint -- src/vs/platform/quickinput/browser/media/quickInput.css`
- `npm run precommit`
- Rendered all 4 `chat/promptFilePickers` fixtures in product and reversed stylesheet order: exact image hashes match with no render errors

title: agents: restore message timestamps from persisted agent transcripts
body:
Chat messages show the time they were sent, but the time disappeared after restarting the client.

## Root cause

The timestamp already flows correctly on the client: `Turn.startedAt` / `Turn.duration` → `stateToProgressAdapter` → `IChatSessionHistoryItem.timestamp` → `ChatRequestModel.requestTimestamp` → renderer. While a session is live, `ChatTurnStarted` actions carry `startedAt`, so times render fine.

The problem is on the agent host: when a session is restored from a persisted transcript, the history **replay mappers** rebuild the turns and dropped the timing entirely. `chatServiceImpl` then passes `message.timestamp ?? null`, and `null` means "unknown, render nothing".

`claudeReplayMapper` already mapped its message timestamps; the Copilot and Codex mappers did not.

## Fix

- **Copilot** (`mapSessionEvents.ts`): read the ISO 8601 `timestamp` off the SDK `SessionEvent` envelope and use it to set `startedAt` and compute `duration`. A parent turn is flushed while handling the event that *starts the next* turn, so the previous event's timestamp is used as its end time — otherwise user idle time between turns would be folded into the previous turn's duration. Malformed/absent timestamps degrade to `undefined` rather than a fabricated time.
- **Codex** (`codexReplayMapper.ts`): derive timing from the persisted thread turn (`startedAt`/`completedAt` are Unix seconds, `durationMs` is preferred when present, mirroring the live `mapTurnCompleted`).

No client change was needed — the client already synthesizes a provisional `Date.now()` timestamp for new requests and renders the host-provided one when available.

## Testing

- New unit tests in `mapSessionEvents.test.ts` and `codexReplayMapper.test.ts`, including a case where envelopes carry no usable timestamp.
- Updated one existing `copilotAgentSession.test.ts` assertion, since replayed turns now carry timing.
- Full `agentHost` suite passes apart from 4 `SessionPermissionManager` failures that are pre-existing on the base commit (verified by stashing) and unrelated to this change.

body: Type: Bug VS Code Version: 1.131.0 (regression — 1.128.0 works) OS Version: Windows 11 x64 ### Summary After auto-updating from 1.128.0 to 1.131.0, all of my MCP servers are started, their tools are enumerated, and then they are **stopped again ~1 second later**. This repeats continuously. Servers are also stopped **while they are still initializing**. This is not just a UI/state annoyance: because the server process is torn down, **stateful MCP servers lose live state**. A Playwright MCP session (live browser) was killed mid-operation. Rolling back to 1.128.0 completely resolves it with no other changes. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure MCP servers in the user `mcp.json` (I have 15). 2. Use VS Code 1.131.0. 3. Watch the MCP output log for any server (`MCP: List Servers` → Show Output). 4. Observe repeated start → `Discovered N tools` → `Stopping server` cycles, with no user action. ### Actual Behaviour From `mcpServer.mcp.config.usrlocal.playwright.log`: ``` 00:16:39.887 [info] Discovered 30 tools 00:17:35.066 [info] Stopping server playwright <-- kills the live browser session 00:17:54.036 [info] Starting server playwright 00:17:59.052 [info] Waiting for server to respond to `initialize` request... 00:18:03.645 [info] Stopping server playwright <-- stopped MID-INITIALIZE 00:18:43.550 [info] Starting server playwright 00:19:05.929 [info] Discovered 30 tools 00:19:21.243 [info] Stopping server playwright ``` All 15 servers are also stopped together within ~5 ms of each other, in two waves ~300 ms apart: ``` 18:27:19.266 [info] Stopping server azure-devops 18:27:19.267 [info] Stopping server binlogmcp 18:27:19.267 [info] Stopping server bluebird-aspaas ... 18:27:19.571 [info] Stopping server azure-devops <-- second wave ``` No extension-host crash/restart is logged around these events, and nothing in my setup issues a stop. ### Expected Behaviour A server that has been started should stay running (as in 1.128.0), and in particular should not be torn down while a tool session is in flight or while it is still responding to `initialize`. ### Notes / What I ruled out - **Not transport-specific.** My servers are `"type": "sse"` pointing at a local bridge. I also reproduced with `"type": "http"` (Streamable HTTP, `/mcp`) — the 404/legacy-SSE fallback message disappears, but the server is still stopped ~1 s after `Discovered N tools`. - **Not the server/bridge.** Direct probes against the same endpoints return HTTP 200 and valid `initialize` results while VS Code shows the server as stopped. - **Not an extension.** Reproduced with only the built-in MCP handling driving the servers. - Tool caches are fully populated (15/15 servers with tools in `mcpToolCache`), yet servers still appear to be treated as needing re-discovery repeatedly. Relevant settings: ```jsonc "chat.mcp.autostart": "newAndOutdated", "chat.mcp.collisionBehavior": "suffix" ``` ### Impact Any MCP server that holds state across calls (browser automation, long-lived sessions, servers with expensive startup or interactive auth) is unusable, because the process can be killed mid-session.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a Django project with `manage.py` in the workspace root.
2. Follow the documented Django unittest setup:
   https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/python/testing#_django-unit-tests
3. Set the required environment variables, including `MANAGE_PY_PATH` and `DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE`.
4. Enable unittest discovery without explicitly configuring `python.testing.unittestArgs`.
5. Open the Testing view or run **Python: Discover Tests**.

## Actual Behaviour

The Python extension runs Django test discovery using:

```text
/Users/kamil/Projects/reactor/.venv/bin/python   /Users/kamil/Projects/reactor/manage.py   test   --testrunner=django_test_runner.CustomDiscoveryTestRunner   -v -s . -p '*test*.py'
```

These appear to be the default arguments intended for Python's standard `unittest discover` command:

```text
-v -s . -p *test*.py
```

They are not valid as-is for Django's `manage.py test` command.

### 1. `-v` is used incorrectly

For Django, `-v` is an alias for `--verbosity` and requires a value:

```text
-v {0,1,2,3}
```

Passing only `-v` therefore causes argument parsing to fail:

```text
manage.py test: error: argument -v/--verbosity: expected one argument
```

### 2. `-s` is not a valid Django test option

Django's `manage.py test` command does not provide a `-s` option.

The `-s .` pair belongs to `python -m unittest discover`, where `-s` specifies the start directory. Passing it to `manage.py test` is therefore incompatible with Django's command-line interface.

## Expected Behaviour

When Django test discovery is enabled through `MANAGE_PY_PATH`, the extension should not pass the default `unittest discover` arguments to `manage.py test`.

Django discovery should work with the documented configuration and without requiring users to override the default test arguments manually.

## Workaround

Explicitly setting an empty argument list makes discovery work:

```json
{
  "python.testing.unittestArgs": []
}
```

## Recommendation

Do not provide any default test arguments when invoking Django's test command.

In other words, when Django discovery is active, the command should be based on:

```shell
python manage.py test --testrunner=django_test_runner.CustomDiscoveryTestRunner
```

Any additional arguments should come only from an explicit user configuration.

This avoids passing options that belong to `unittest discover` but have different meanings, require different values, or do not exist in Django's test command.

## Relevant Log

2026-07-29 08:27:41.797 [error] usage: manage.py test [-h] [--noinput] [--testrunner TESTRUNNER] [--failfast]

title: Fix Persian and Arabic Rendering in the VS Code Integrated Terminal
body:
# Fix Persian and Arabic Rendering in the VS Code Integrated Terminal

<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: 1.130.0
- OS Version: macOS (Apple Silicon)

## Description

The VS Code integrated terminal does not properly render Persian (Farsi) and Arabic text.

Persian and Arabic languages require proper RTL (right-to-left) and BiDi (bidirectional) text handling, but the integrated terminal currently has several rendering issues.

## Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open VS Code integrated terminal.
2. Run:

```bash
echo "سلام دنیا"
```

3. Observe the output.

## Actual Behavior:

- Persian and Arabic characters are not rendered correctly.
- Characters may appear disconnected or in the wrong order.
- RTL text direction is not handled properly.
- Mixed Persian/Arabic and English text is displayed incorrectly.
- Cursor position does not always match the visual position of the text.
- Text selection and copy/paste behavior can become inconsistent.

## Expected Behavior:

The integrated terminal should correctly render RTL languages such as Persian and Arabic, including:

- Proper character shaping.
- Correct right-to-left text direction.
- Correct handling of mixed RTL/LTR content.
- Accurate cursor movement and text selection.

## Additional Information:

Tested with UTF-8 locale:

LANG=C.UTF-8
LC_CTYPE=C.UTF-8

The problem is not related to encoding.

Extensions that implement an RTL rendering layer can partially solve the issue, suggesting that the main limitation is related to the terminal rendering engine.

It would be great to have native RTL and Arabic shaping support in the VS Code integrated terminal.

Thank you for your work on improving the terminal experience.

title: Make opus48 prompt always-on and remove gating setting
body:
Remove the `Opus48Prompt` config key and setting. The opus48 system-prompt overrides now apply unconditionally for opus48 models, with tool-aware content (e.g. the `problems` tool is only named when the session has it).

The prompt text is the `vscode-on-ahp` variant from the agent-host token-efficiency report — the VS Code system prompt ported onto the agent host, with the report's recommendations applied. Instead of `mode: 'replace'`, it uses `customize` with `action: 'replace'` on every instruction-bearing section, so repository custom instructions, session context, the git co-author trailer and the registry's composition layer (file-link contract, gated browser line, tool-search lines) all still apply.

## Before → after, by section

"Before" is what an Opus 4.8 session gets on `main` today: the SDK foundation prompt with only `identity` replaced. The overrides in brackets applied only when `chat.agentHost.opus48Prompt.enabled` was turned on, which defaulted to `false`.

| Section | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `identity` (group: preamble + `tone` + `tool_efficiency`) | agent-host identity string only | agent-host identity + content-policy lines + `<instructions>` + `<parallelization_strategy>` + `<delegation>` + `<communication_style>`. Replacing the group drops its SDK siblings, so this section now owns tone and tool-efficiency guidance outright |
| `tone` | SDK default *[+ appended "provide concise, focused responses…" line]* | folded into `<communication_style>`: target 1–3 sentences, no preamble/recap, no emoji, lead each new phase with one line |
| `code_change_rules` | SDK default | `<implementation_discipline>` (no over-engineering, no unrequested docs/comments, no scratch markdown files) + `<verification>` (`problems` first, build only when it is clean — gated on the tool) + `<dependency_policy>` (do not install packages to repair an unrelated environment) |
| `guidelines` | SDK default *[+ two subagent fan-out lines]* | `<task_tracking>` (session `todos`/`todo_deps` via `sql`; skip for single-step work). The fan-out lines are replaced by `<delegation>` in `identity`, which pushes the opposite way — delegate less, not more |
| `safety` | SDK default | environment limitations (shared environment, disable pagers, confidential-instruction rules) + `<security_requirements>` (OWASP, prompt-injection vigilance) + `<operational_safety>` (confirm destructive/shared-system actions, `kill <PID>` only, refuse obfuscated shell expansion) |
| `tool_instructions` | SDK default + registry-composed gated lines | `<tool_use_instructions>`: prefer `grep`/`glob`/`view`(/`usages`) over shell equivalents, `view_range` and the 20 KB truncation, each shell call is a fresh process, combine independent inspection commands into one call, `shellId` instead of re-running, `ask_user` instead of asking in prose, absolute paths, real JSON for object parameters. Plus `<notebook_instructions>`, gated on the notebook tools. The registry still composes the browser line and tool-search lines on top |
| `last_instructions` | SDK default (parallel tool calling, persistence, task completion) | `<output_formatting>` (markdown, backticked symbols, KaTeX, mermaid). Persistence/completion moves to `<verification>`; the file-link contract is still appended by the registry |
| `environment_context`, `custom_instructions`, `runtime_instructions` | SDK default | unchanged — they carry session facts, not guidance |
| Gating | `chat.agentHost.opus48Prompt.enabled`, default `false` | none — always on for `claude-opus-4-8` / `claude-opus-4.8` |

## What actually changed in behavior terms

| Change | Rationale |
|---|---|
| **Added** `<verification>` with `problems` before builds | The stock prompt called `problems` **0 times across 702 benchmark instances** while running a build or test on 69% of tasks. A diagnostics call is one cheap round-trip; a build is a step plus a large tool result plus, often, a package install |
| **Added** `<dependency_policy>` | The stock rule permitted installing "after a missing-dependency failure", which is the exact loop it was meant to stop |
| **Added** explicit batching in `<parallelization_strategy>` and "combine independent inspection commands into a single shell call" | Steps are the dominant cost — each one re-sends the whole prefix. This line is the replacement that was missing from the measured build; see caveats |
| **Added** harness facts the model cannot infer: fresh-process shell, `shellId`, `view_range`, 20 KB truncation, `ask_user`, detached background processes | Carried from the CLI prompt. Under the agent host the agent prefixes `cd ` on 95.6% of shell calls, so it visibly depends on knowing this |
| **Removed** memory instructions, `<code_search_tools>`, and the inline `<sql>`/`<task>` tool documentation | No memory tool and no semantic search on this harness; `sql` was used on 0.3% of tasks and `task` on 0.0%, at ~1,700 tokens re-sent every step |
| **Removed** most exploration braking | The stock prompt carried 9 units of braking against 1 of acceleration, and the agent explored **19–21% more** than the VS Code harness anyway. Measured non-binding, so it was paying rent on every step |
| **Not added**: more brakes, anti-verbosity rules, anti-over-engineering rules, read-before-edit rules | All measured as already-satisfied: the agent adds less context per step (404 vs 485 tokens), re-reads less (0.72 vs 0.93 files) and writes 25–85% smaller diffs than the VS Code harness at equal or better pass rates |

Net effect on the wire: the system prompt drops from ~26,100 to ~15,600 characters.

## Evidence

`claude-opus-4.8`, agent-host harness. Figures re-derived from Kusto (`CESBenchmarkMetricsV2View`, `CESBenchmarkTrajectoriesTable`) and cross-checked against server-priced `Cost_Total_USD` (nano-AIU, ~100% coverage) rather than a token proxy alone.

| Benchmark | Arm | Runs | Pass rate | Cost / instance (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| refactorbench (117 inst.) | prompt under test | 4 | 67.7% | **$0.302** |
| refactorbench | stock, same-day build | 1 | 68.4% | $0.410 (**−26%**) |
| refactorbench | stock, earlier builds | 3 + 3 | 68.7% / 67.8% | $0.382 / $0.421 (**−21% / −28%**) |
| terminalbench2-1 (89 inst.) | prompt under test | 3 | 80.9% | **$1.09** |
| terminalbench2-1 | stock | 9 priced | 83.3% (same build) / 82.6% (all 15) | $1.16 (**−6%** aggregate, **−21%** median instance) |

Mechanism on refactorbench, per instance: `problems` **0 → 0.6** calls, package installs **94 → 46** across 117 instances, steps **12.7 → 11.2**, and 104/117 instances got cheaper (median −26%).

Run IDs — treatment: `30478289378`, `30489880150`, `30489883996`, `30489887754` (rb); `30479128444`, `30479133718`, `30479139169` (tb). Baselines: `30429462238`, `30210138422/36546/34390`, `30190081881/80129/77172` (rb); 15 stock runs (tb).

## SDK content the section replacements drop

`identity` and `last_instructions` are section *groups*; replacing them also drops their siblings. Confirmed by reading the runtime's section map (`@github/copilot` → `hLn`) rather than inferred:

| Dropped | Section | Keep? |
|---|---|---|
| `model_information` — "Powered by `<model name=… id=…/>`. When asked which model you are … reply with 'I'm powered by …'. If the model was changed during the conversation, acknowledge the change" | `identity` | **Yes.** The agent can no longer answer "which model are you?". The ported prompt had a line for this ("state the model you are running as") but it was dropped when the identity line was swapped for `COPILOT_AGENT_HOST_IDENTITY`, so the loss is double |
| `version_information` — "Version number: X" | `identity` | Probably — cheap, and users ask |
| `task_instructions` — "Your job is to perform the task the user requested." | `identity` | Low value, superseded |
| `search_and_delegation` and `tool_efficiency` | `identity` | Partly re-added by hand, but the SDK versions are **session-resolved** — they interpolate the actual `glob`/`grep`/shell tool names and emit "chain related commands with `&&`" only when the shell supports it. The hand-written replacements hardcode `grep`/`glob`/`view` |
| `quality_and_persistence` — "deliver complete, working solutions … don't settle for partial fixes. Verify your changes actually work before considering the task done." | `last_instructions` | No — overlaps `<verification>` |
| `task_completion` instructions | `last_instructions` | **No.** The `task_complete` tool is registered only when autopilot is active (`p.autopilotActive && B.push(Nce(p))`), while these instructions render unconditionally — so outside autopilot they described a tool that isn't in the session. Under autopilot, the autopilot instructions in `runtime_instructions` (preserved) already cover when and how to call it |
| "Respond concisely to the user, but be thorough in your work." | `last_instructions` | No — overlaps `<communication_style>` |
| Guidelines *tips* block | `guidelines` | **No.** Four of its five tips are already restated by this PR (clean up temp files, no markdown notes, prefer editing over creating, use `ask_user`); keeping both would duplicate them |
| Rubber-duck experiment instructions | `guidelines` | **Decision needed.** `rubberDuck` is a real forwarded config key, and its prompt lines are composed into `guidelines` — so enabling it on an Opus 4.8 session now has no prompt effect. Either accept that Opus 4.8 opts out, or re-add the gated lines |
| Sandbox-aware environment limitations | `safety` | **Bug.** The SDK picks sandboxed vs unsandboxed text from the live sandbox config. The replacement hardcodes *"You are not operating in a sandbox dedicated to this task"*, which is false whenever `chat.agentHost.sdkSandbox.enabled` is `on`/`allowNetwork` |

Not affected, verified: the git co-author trailer, system-notification instructions, plan-mode/autopilot instructions, memories and session context all render into `runtime_instructions`, which this PR leaves alone.

## Caveats and follow-ups

- **This is not literally the build that was measured.** The measured build was missing five lines (including "Always validate that your changes don't break existing behavior") and shipped the shell-batching recommendation as a deletion with no replacement. This PR restores all of them, so the text here is a superset of what the numbers above were produced on.
- **Terminalbench shows a real ~2pt regression that the prompt has not been cleared of.** Detail below.
- **Both benchmarks are headless, single-shot coding tasks.** Nothing here measures interactive-chat verbosity, proactiveness, formatting, security or memory behavior, and this prompt changes all of those. Worth a manual pass on ordinary chat before and after.

### Terminalbench regression — what the instance-level data says

Two of the 13 regressed instances are **infrastructure**, not the prompt: `build-pmars` and `qemu-alpine-ssh` each hit `TimeoutError: @vscode/test-electron request timeout out after 15000ms`, produced no trajectory and no agent output at all. Excluding those instance-runs:

| Comparator | NEW | BASE | Δ | exact permutation p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| same build (1.132, 6 runs), infra excluded | 81.5% | 83.5% | **−2.0pt** | **0.036** |
| same build, infra included | 80.9% | 83.3% | −2.4pt | 0.048 |
| all 15 baselines (3 builds), infra included | 80.9% | 82.6% | −1.7pt | 0.097 |

So the regression is marginally significant against the same-build comparator and not significant against the pooled one. Per-instance it is diffuse: 13 regressed, 10 improved, and **no single instance survives Benjamini-Hochberg correction** (best is `build-pmars` at p=0.083 uncorrected — and that one is the infra failure).

The "agent stopped inspecting and hammered the shell" mechanism does **not** hold up as the explanation. Splitting `view` calls by outcome group, the drop is largest in the instances whose result did not change:

| Group | `view` base → new | `bash` base → new |
|---|---|---|
| regressed (13) | 4.52 → 3.71 (−18%) | 22.5 → 25.1 (+11%) |
| improved (10) | 3.57 → 4.00 (+12%) | 14.9 → 14.5 (−3%) |
| unchanged (66) | 3.84 → 2.83 (**−26%**) | 11.3 → 12.2 (+8%) |

Reduced inspection is an arm-wide prompt effect that is uncorrelated with pass/fail. Reading the failures directly, the genuine ones look task-specific rather than disciplinary — `gcode-to-text` produced `flag{gc00d3_iz_ch4LLenGiNg}` against an expected `flag{gc0d3_iz_ch4LLenGiNg}`, a single-character perception error.

**Conclusion: the ~2pt drop is real but unattributed.** It is not explained by infra, not localized to any instance, and not explained by the inspection-rate change. Three treatment runs is too few to resolve a 2pt effect against a baseline with sd 1.1. The confirmation run should be sized to settle this rather than treated as a formality.

Also note the treatment arm is a single commit (`477b625`) while the six baselines span four commits, so build and prompt are confounded by construction.

title: Terminal in an auxiliary window stops rendering on U+2591: custom glyph rasterizer calls createElement in a child window

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

body:
## Summary

In a terminal that has been moved into a separate window, any output containing
U+2591 LIGHT SHADE (or its U+2592 / U+2593 neighbours) permanently stops that
terminal from painting. Keys still reach the program and it keeps running; only
the drawing dies.

The cause is an uncaught exception, not slowness:

```
Uncaught Error: Not allowed to create elements in child window JavaScript context.
    Always use the main window so that "xyz instanceof HTMLElement" continues to work.
    at e.document.createElement (auxiliaryWindowService.ts:408:1)
    at CustomGlyphRasterizer.ts:461:48
    at a (CustomGlyphRasterizer.ts:82:7)
    at e.tryDrawCustomGlyph (CustomGlyphRasterizer.ts:35:7)
    at _._drawToCache (TextureAtlas.ts:533:21)
    at _._getFromCacheMap (TextureAtlas.ts:283:21)
    at _.getRasterizedGlyph (TextureAtlas.ts:266:17)
    at d._updateCell (GlyphRenderer.ts:246:28)
    at d.updateCell (GlyphRenderer.ts:225:10)
    at M._updateModel (WebglRenderer.ts:592:36)
    at M.renderRows (WebglRenderer.ts:382:12)
    at d._renderRows (RenderService.ts:203:26)
    at t.RenderDebouncer._renderCallback (RenderService.ts:74:70)
    at t.RenderDebouncer._innerRefresh (RenderDebouncer.ts:72:10)
```

`drawPatternChar` in `CustomGlyphRasterizer.ts` is reached only by the
`BLOCK_PATTERN` glyph type, which is the three shade characters and nothing else.
It builds its stipple by creating a temporary canvas:

```ts
const tmpCanvas = ctx.canvas.ownerDocument.createElement('canvas');
```

In an auxiliary window that `ownerDocument` is the child window's document, and
`auxiliaryWindowService` replaces `createElement` there with a function that
throws. The exception escapes through `_updateModel`'s cell loop, so the render
pass aborts partway and every later attempt aborts at the same cell.

That is directly visible on screen: rows paint normally up to the first shade
character and stop there mid-row. It is not a progressive slowdown; it is a cell
loop that never gets past that cell again.

Other block-element and box-drawing characters are unaffected, because their
glyph types (`SOLID_OCTANT_BLOCK_VECTOR`, `PATH_FUNCTION`) draw straight onto the
existing canvas and never call `createElement`.

## Environment

- VS Code 1.130.0 (stable, commit `1b6a188127eeaf9194f945eb6eb89a657e93c54c`,
  built 2026-07-22), bundling `@xterm/xterm` 6.1.0-beta.288
- **Terminal moved into a separate window.** Required: the guard that throws
  exists only for child windows, and the terminal this was found in is always
  run popped out
- WebGL renderer (`terminal.integrated.gpuAcceleration` at its default)
- `terminal.integrated.customGlyphs` at its default of `true`
- Terminal 344 columns x 77 rows
- Renderer host: Windows 11, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 980 Ti (6 GB)
- Shell host: Linux 6.8.0-48-generic, over VS Code Remote

## Reproduction

1. Open a terminal and move it into a new window (Terminal: Move Terminal into
   New Window).
2. Run the script below with `python3 shade-repro.py 2591 2>/tmp/frames.log`.
3. The screen stops painting immediately, part-way through a row. The DevTools
   console for that window fills with the error above, one per render attempt.
   `/tmp/frames.log` keeps growing once a second, so the process is fine.
4. Ctrl-C still works even though nothing is drawn.
5. `python3 shade-repro.py 2500` and `python3 shade-repro.py 2588` both paint all
   300 frames normally in the same window.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Repaint a screenful of one character once a second and see if the terminal
keeps up.

    python3 shade-repro.py 2591 2>/tmp/frames.log     # stops painting
    python3 shade-repro.py 2500 2>/tmp/frames.log     # fine
    python3 shade-repro.py 2588 2>/tmp/frames.log     # fine
    python3 shade-repro.py 0058 2>/tmp/frames.log     # 'X', control

Optional row and column counts set how many copies each frame carries.

Rows 1-10 are the character under test. Row 12 carries a frame counter and a
wall clock, which are the liveness signal: while the terminal is painting they
advance every second, and when it stops painting they freeze mid-stride.

Every frame is also written to stderr, so redirect that to a file. When the
screen has frozen, the log still growing is what shows the process is fine and
only the painting has stopped.

Press Ctrl-C to stop. Input keeps working while the screen is frozen.
"""

import signal
import sys
import time

CODEPOINT = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "2591"
CH = chr(int(CODEPOINT, 16))
ROWS = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 10
COLS = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 100
FRAMES = 300


# Leave the alternate screen and restore the cursor even when killed, so a
# `timeout` or a `kill` does not strand the terminal.
def stop(signum, frame):
    raise KeyboardInterrupt


signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, stop)
signal.signal(signal.SIGHUP, stop)

# A few 256-colour indices, because a real TUI colours its output.
COLOURS = (78, 214, 203, 245)

sys.stdout.write("\033[?1049h\033[?25l")
try:
    for n in range(1, FRAMES + 1):
        out = ["\033[H"]
        for r in range(ROWS):
            out.append(f"\033[38;5;{COLOURS[r % len(COLOURS)]}m")
            out.append(CH * COLS)
            out.append("\033[0m\033[K\r\n")
        out.append(
            f"\033[{ROWS + 2};1HU+{CODEPOINT.upper()}   frame {n}/{FRAMES}   "
            f"clock {time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}   [ctrl-c] quit\033[K"
        )
        sys.stdout.write("".join(out))
        sys.stdout.flush()
        print(f"{n} {time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
        time.sleep(1)
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    pass
finally:
    sys.stdout.write("\033[?1049l\033[?25h")
    sys.stdout.flush()
```

## How the character was narrowed down

Before the console error was found, the trigger was isolated by replaying one
captured frame with a single property changed at a time. Included because it
rules out several plausible-looking causes:

| frame contains | result |
| --- | --- |
| 57 x U+2591 LIGHT SHADE | stops painting |
| 145 x U+2500 BOX DRAWINGS LIGHT HORIZONTAL | fine |
| 19 x U+2588 FULL BLOCK | fine |
| 432 SGR colour sequences, no non-ASCII | fine |
| ASCII text and cursor addressing only | fine |
| U+25AE / U+25AF vertical rectangles | fine |

- **Not font coverage.** Reproduces on fonts that contain U+2591, Cascadia Code
  among them. Consistent with the custom-glyph path, where the font is never
  consulted.
- **Not East Asian width.** U+2591 is Narrow; U+2588, which works, is Ambiguous.
- **Not the multiplexer or the pty.** Reproduces with no tmux involved. While one
  window was affected, a separate tmux client attached to the same window
  streamed 64 KB with zero discards and drew every glyph correctly.
- **Not renderer load.** A performance profile taken while the screen was frozen
  showed no long task and no hot stack, which is what sent us to the console.

## Workarounds

All three work:

- Move the terminal back into the main window. The guard only applies to child
  windows.
- `terminal.integrated.customGlyphs: false` — keeps GPU acceleration and stops
  the custom-glyph rasterizer for the Block Elements range. Verified with the
  script above: 300 frames of U+2591 paint cleanly with it off, and the screen
  stops immediately with it on.
- `terminal.integrated.gpuAcceleration: "off"` — the WebGL addon never loads, so
  the custom-glyph path cannot run.

## Suggested fix

`drawPatternChar` does not need a DOM canvas. Building the pattern on an
`OffscreenCanvas` would avoid `createElement` entirely and so avoid the child
window guard — the same move already made for `WidthCache` in xterm.js #5549
("Use OffscreenCanvas over DOM for WidthCache").

Separately, an exception thrown while rasterizing one glyph currently takes down
the whole render pass for good. Catching it per glyph, and falling back to the
font for that character, would turn this class of failure into a cosmetic
problem rather than a dead terminal.

## Searched first

No existing report found for shade characters, `BLOCK_PATTERN`, or custom-glyph
rendering in auxiliary windows. Nearest are xterm.js #2409 (the original request
that introduced custom glyph drawing) and #5480 (moving the `customGlyphs`
option into the WebGL addon), neither about this. xterm.js #5548 (`WidthCache`
layout thrashing) is a different bug and its fix is already in this bundle.
